title: <= on the naturals is transitive
statement: For natural numbers a, b and c, if a <= b and b <= c, then a <= c.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.le_trans : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat.le x0 x1) -> ((x4 : AxNat.le x1 x2) -> AxNat.le x0 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.le_trans is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.le_trans 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.le_trans[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check; the command both performs it and prints the admitted type, which is copied verbatim into formal.statement.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `nat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0`, over the FULL trusted surface rather than Declaration::Axiom alone. The enumeration is per-environment, not per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type.

notes: depends_on is literal, read off theorem_dependency_inventory's direct-edge output for this theorem (cross-checked against nat_theorem_inventory's own admitted type), keeping only edges whose target is itself a registered fact. No theorem dependencies (decided directly over the order's recursive definition); it is itself a direct dependency of Nat.le_of_succ_le_succ, Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt and Nat.mul_le_mul_left in this kernel.
